correctness.rationale: An explicit Laplacian orbit decomposition gives 2(s-2) copies of u+(s-1)v, one copy of su, a trivial zero, and two remaining eigenvalues with sum su+2t and product 2tu. The Kemeny reciprocal sum therefore equals 2(s-2)/(u+(s-1)v)+(s+1)/(su)+s/(2t). Strict trace-inverse convexity and injective edge weighting force a unique automorphism-invariant global optimizer; monotonicity saturates t and v; a strictly positive scalar second derivative and endpoint derivatives prove one unique optimal u. Rescaling x=su yields the limiting bridge sqrt(2)-1 and optimal K/s=7/2+sqrt(2). Direct exact-rational full Laplacian inversions and numeric asymptotics replay in verify.py.

originality.rationale: Compared the actual mathematical statements of the primary papers and relevant indexed graph-family results. The general reversible Kemeny SDP, the fixed simple-walk barbell Kemeny formula, and SLEM-optimized walks do not state or directly imply the exact unrestricted equal-clique-barbell probability allocation and its asymptotic bridge constant. The new result requires a nontrivial eigenmode reduction and asymptotic minimizer localization. Search incompleteness and possible unindexed equivalent calculations remain explicit risks.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent exact Kemeny-optimal barbell calculation may exist in a specialized graph or stochastic-control reference.
A generic optimization theorem can be numerically specialized to these graphs; the contribution is the explicit analytic family solution, not computational solvability.
The complete literature on degree-heterogeneous and constrained stationary policies was not exhaustively surveyed.

value.rationale: A barbell is a canonical dense-community network with a single severe bottleneck. The solution classifies the unrestricted globally optimal uniform-stationary symmetric transition policy for every equal clique size, proves that the bottleneck receives a constant limiting probability rather than a vanishing probability, and derives a linear-in-size Kemeny regret for the standard maximum-degree walk. This is a structural, quantitative optimization benchmark rather than a routine reparameterization or a marginal numerical improvement.
